body:
`food_kg_factors` exempts rows that record no unit at all from the price-ratio inference (GH #874, `0554ec907`): *"`u='Unknown'` is the absence of a unit, so it gets no inferred kg."* The exemption is keyed on a spelling set:

```python
# transformations.py:3336
_U_SENTINELS = frozenset({U_UNKNOWN.lower(), 'manquant'})   # -> {'unknown', 'manquant'}
```

**Uganda writes `'---'`**, at `countries/Uganda/_/uganda.py:310` (`unitlabels[int_k] = '---'`). Measured:

| | |
|---|---|
| Uganda `food_acquired` rows with `u == 'Unknown'` | **0** |
| rows with `u == '---'` | **7,359** |
| rows `_unit_sentinel_mask` catches | **0 of 355,571** |
| `'---'` rows it catches | **0 of 7,359** |

So #874's exemption is a **complete no-op for Uganda**, and its own comment -- *"Niger and Uganda already write this sentinel"* -- is false for Uganda. Niger does (`niger.py:496`, `U_NA = 'Unknown'`); Uganda does not.

## What the rows get instead

The inference reaches them and mints a factor on the u-pooled `unit` rung -- one kilogram-per-nothing for the whole country:

```
i           t        j                   u    s          kg_per_unit  KgFactorSource
1013000210  2005-06  Restaurant (food)   ---  inkind     0.064583     unit
1013000211  2005-06  Other Juice         ---  purchased  0.064583     unit
1021000102  2005-06  Other Foods         ---  purchased  0.064583     unit
```

`'---'` is not an obscure label -- **`local_tools.py:1721` states the repo's own convention for it**: *"we assume that cells with the string '---' should be null"*, and `:1776` does `df.replace({'---': pd.NA})`. One layer reads it as null; the unit layer reads it as a unit and weighs it.

## Which items this hits

`'---'` dominates exactly the categories bought by **value**, not by measure -- `Restaurant (food)` carries it on **4,769 of 6,271** rows, alongside `Other Foods` and `Other Juice`. A prepared restaurant meal has no kilogram to infer, and the survey did not record one.

## How it surfaced

Uganda `var/nutrition.parquet` fails `tests/test_uganda_invariance.py` on `content_hash`: 23,284 of 23,801 rows changed, Energy -18.7%, and `Restaurant (food)` was the largest single mover in `food_quantities` (-97.6%). Three hypotheses were tested directly:

| hypothesis | result |
|---|---|
| unit work changed quantities | **confirmed** -- `food_quantities` total 1.4579e6 -> 1.2424e6, **-14.78%**, matching #850's published Uganda figure exactly; row count unchanged |
| label changes altered FCT matching | **refuted** -- distinct `j` 129 -> 129, none added, none removed |
| `food_expenditures` should be unaffected | **confirmed** -- 247,049 rows and total 7.263e8 both unchanged to +0.00% |

So the whole delta is kg-side, and this sentinel gap is part of it.

## Fix

Add Uganda's spelling to `_U_SENTINELS`, or better, stop keying on spellings: `'---'` is already the repo's documented null marker, so the country module should write `U_UNKNOWN` (or `pd.NA`) rather than a string one layer treats as null and another as a unit. A test should assert that every `u` spelling the corpus actually carries is either a real unit or in the sentinel set -- the present arrangement is a **spelling allowlist that fails open**, which is the same shape as the `savio_venv.sh` glob fixed in `d72054a7d`.

## Not yet measured

Two of my Restaurant-kg figures disagree (6,240 kg from a direct `j` filter vs 10.59 from a `groupby(level='j')` sweep), so **treat the per-item magnitude as unverified** pending one clean measurement. The mechanism above is verified from the code and the row counts and does not depend on it.
title: Uganda's no-unit sentinel is spelled '---', which `_U_SENTINELS` does not know, so 7,359 unitless rows are given an invented kg factor (GH #874 is a no-op for Uganda)

Workplan from a review of the venv setup, prompted by the question of running several sucoder slices on **different Savio nodes** against one shared mirror simultaneously. Filing it as a tracker because the pieces have an order and two of them are decisions rather than tasks.

## The frame

The venv is three layers with three different scopes, and two of them are currently stored in a shared place:

| layer | correct scope | stored today | result with N nodes |
|---|---|---|---|
| dependency closure | global | `.venv.sqfs` on Lustre | fine |
| FUSE mount | per job | `/local/job$ID/venv_img` | fine |
| `.venv` symlink | **per clone** | the **mirror's** `.venv` | last writer wins; the other N-1 dangle |
| editable `lsms_library` path | **per clone** | the `.pth` **inside the image** | `python <script>.py` runs the mirror, not your tree |

One bug, twice: per-clone state kept in a shared location. A single node hides it.

Multi-node **strengthens** the squashfs image over the alternatives — one Lustre inode with N cheap mounts beats N independent unlocked resolves that silently diverge. The image is the right artifact; what needs removing is the per-clone state baked into it.

## Rule that falls out

**Clones across nodes, worktrees within a node.** A `/local` worktree of the Lustre mirror puts its index and `HEAD` in `$MIRROR/.git/worktrees/<name>/` — shared mutable state registered at a path no other node can see — and, more to the point, a worktree has **no push step**, so it bypasses the post-commit publish, the `REJECTED`/`pull --ff-only` path and the per-job WIP ref that the durability story is built on. Within a node, worktrees of the `/local` clone are entirely node-local and fine.

## The pieces

| | what | kind |
|---|---|---|
| #957 | the image's editable install names the mirror; `__version__` 2060 commits stale | fix + one decision |
| #958 | `savio_venv.sh` and the mirror's `.venv` symlink assume one node | fix |
| #959 | no tracked lock file | decision |
| #960 | the venv docs describe one node and one checkout | docs |
| ligon/sucoder#27 | per-job warn state exists; agents are told to poll the per-mirror copy | sucoder |
| ligon/sucoder#28 | generated burst guidance reads the mirror's checked-out branch | sucoder |

## Order

**#957 then #958**, in that order and close together: #957 strips the editable install out of the master, and #958's `update` is what re-images it — so #958 should land the guard that refuses to image a master still carrying `lsms_library.pth`, or the next `poetry install` puts it straight back. #960 can go alongside either. #959 is independent and is a decision to make rather than work to schedule; the provenance it needed is already captured (9c5e2081e, `slurm_logs/venv_provenance/`).

The two sucoder issues are independent of all of the above.

## Two decisions for @ligon

1. **#957** — strip the `.pth` only, or `pip uninstall lsms_library` (which also removes the dist-info and drops `__version__` to `"0.0.0"`, uninformative rather than wrong).
2. **#959** — pin the lock to what the warm corpus was built under, or resolve fresh and pair it with a deliberate cold re-warm. They are different lock files and only the second is a single command.

## What was measured, so it does not have to be re-measured

On n0035.savio4, 2026-09-21, with `.venv.sqfs` hand-mounted:

- The import table in #957 — `python <script>.py` is the trap; `pytest` and `python -c` from the clone are accidentally correct.
- `flock` works on the Lustre mirror and on `/local`; it fails under `$HOME` (NFS, `OSError [Errno 37]`). The parquet cache is symlinked to Lustre, so it locks.
- Parquet cache writes are already atomic (PID+uuid temp then `os.replace`, same directory, `local_tools.py:1962-1975`), so the shared cache is multi-writer-safe across nodes.
- The squashfs mount prerequisites hold on savio4, not just savio2/3.
- `/local` job directories are reaped, not persistent (link count 2 on old stubs) — which settles the contradiction between the two venv documents and kills the adopt-or-build recipe.
- Outbound network works from a compute node (pypi and github, ~0.2 s), so a lock can be generated here.
title: [tracking] The venv layering assumes one node, one checkout and one job -- workplan for simultaneous multi-node work

`/poetry.lock` is gitignored (`.gitignore:37`) and no lock is tracked (`git ls-files` has none). `pyproject.toml` pins only open ranges — `pandas >=3.0`, `pyarrow (>=21.0.0)`, `CFEDemands>=0.10.0`, `ligonlibrary (>=0.2.0)`.

@ligon confirms this is not intentional.

So until today the only record of the environment the warm parquet corpus was built under was the unversioned master venv at `~/mirrors/LSMS_Library/.venv.lustre`, which any session can `pip install` into. `SkunkWorks/savio_venv.md` states that "`pyproject.toml`/`poetry.lock` remain the tracked source of truth for what the venv contains" — that is not true today, and the doc correction is #960.

## Provenance is now captured

Committed in 9c5e2081e as `slurm_logs/venv_provenance/`: a 247-package `pip freeze` of the master plus a README recording what it does and does not say.

| package | version |
|---|---|
| python | 3.11.6 |
| pandas | 3.0.2 |
| numpy | 2.4.4 |
| pyarrow | 23.0.1 |
| scipy | 1.17.1 |
| dvc | 3.67.1 |

Three caveats written up there: the freeze's editable line reports the mirror's git HEAD dynamically rather than a pinned version; the dist-info version is frozen at install time and is wrong (#957); and `lsms==0.4.13` is still installed although `pyproject.toml` retired it (`CLAUDE.md`, "the `lsms` upstream dependency has been retired") — inert, but drift between the master and the tracked spec.

## The decision, and why it is not one command

Two options that produce different lock files:

**A. Pin to what the corpus was built under.** Records the environment that actually produced the warm caches; costs no rebuild. But poetry has no constraints-file concept, so this is not `poetry lock` with a flag — it means editing `pyproject.toml` toward the frozen versions, or `poetry add pkg==x` per package, or moving to `uv lock`, which does honour `[tool.uv] constraint-dependencies`. A realistic middle path is to run `poetry lock` fresh, diff it against the freeze, and adjudicate only where they differ.

**B. Fresh resolve.** `poetry lock` against the open ranges. Cleaner, but it will move versions, and dependency versions are deliberately **not** folded into `build_transforms_fingerprint` — so a move changes results with **no cache invalidation**. It should be paired with a deliberate cold re-warm, not done casually.

Whichever, drop `/poetry.lock` from `.gitignore` and commit the result. Outbound network works from a savio4 compute node (pypi and github both answered in ~0.2s from n0035.savio4), so this does not need a login node.

Multi-node raises the stakes: N nodes means more chance someone rebuilds the image, and the lock is the only thing that makes a rebuild reproducible.
title: No lock file is tracked (/poetry.lock is gitignored), so nothing records the environment the warm parquet corpus was built under

`bin/savio_venv.sh` and the `.venv` symlink both assume there is one node, one checkout and one job. With sucoder's local-disk tiering that is already false on a single node, and with simultaneous work on several nodes it breaks outright.

## The frame

The venv has three layers with three different scopes. Two of them are stored in a shared place:

| layer | correct scope | stored today | result with N nodes |
|---|---|---|---|
| dependency closure | global | `.venv.sqfs` on Lustre | fine |
| FUSE mount | per job | `/local/job$ID/venv_img` | fine |
| `.venv` symlink | **per clone** | the **mirror's** `.venv` | last writer wins; the other N-1 dangle |
| editable `lsms_library` path | **per clone** | the `.pth` **inside the image** | see #957 |

Both breakages are one bug: per-clone state kept in a shared location. One node hides it.

## Four concrete defects

**1. `REPO` conflates the image's location with the symlink's target.** `savio_venv.sh:24` derives both from `$BASH_SOURCE/..`. Run from a `/local` clone, `MASTER` and `IMG` resolve to `<clone>/.venv.lustre` and `<clone>/.venv.sqfs`, neither of which exists — all three are gitignored (`.gitignore:18-21`) so the clone never receives them — and `mount` dies `no image at ...`. The script is currently only runnable from the mirror.

**2. The mirror's `.venv` symlink is shared mutable state.** `savio_venv.sh:73` does `ln -sfn "$mnt" "$REPO/.venv"`. Node A points it at `/local/jobA/venv_img`; node B then points it at `/local/jobB/venv_img`, a path that does not exist on node A. It is currently dangling (`-> /local/job39008163/venv_img`; that job ran on n0244.savio4).

It should be retired rather than fixed. It is a relic of working directly in the mirror; each clone should own its own symlink, pointing at its own job's mount.

**3. `update` needs a lock.** It `pip install`s into `.venv.lustre` on shared Lustre and then images it. Two nodes doing that concurrently corrupts the master. `flock` works on the mirror (verified on Lustre; it does **not** work under `$HOME`, which is NFS — `OSError [Errno 37] No locks available`), so an `flock` around the whole master-mutation-plus-image is available and cheap.

**4. Nothing records which image generation a mount is on.** The `mv -f "$IMG.tmp.$$" "$IMG"` swap at `savio_venv.sh:47` is atomic and running mounts keep the old inode — that part is good, and it is exactly what makes multi-node safe. But the consequence is that two nodes can legitimately be running different venv generations at once with nothing to say so. A generation id stamped into the image, printed by `mount`, closes that.

## Verified on savio4

`SkunkWorks/savio_venv.md` claims the mount prerequisites hold "on Savio savio2/savio3 as of 2026-06". They also hold on savio4, measured on n0035.savio4 today: `/dev/fuse` is world-RW, `/usr/libexec/apptainer/bin/squashfuse_ll` is present, `/usr/bin/fusermount` is the setuid fuse2 binary the `fusermount3` shim needs, and the venv's base interpreter (`.../python-3.11.6/.../bin/python3.11`, from `pyvenv.cfg`) exists. A hand-run mount of `.venv.sqfs` succeeded and imported the library.

## Also: the image is stale against its master

`.venv.sqfs` was imaged 2026-09-07 16:23; `.venv.lustre/lib/python3.11/site-packages` was last written 2026-09-07 23:15, seven hours later. The delta is `dunamai 1.26.2` and `poetry-dynamic-versioning 1.10.0`. That affects cutting a wheel, not running the library, but it means the image is not currently a faithful copy of the master and one `update` is owed.

Related: #957 (the `.pth`, which must be stripped before the next image is built), #960 (docs).
title: bin/savio_venv.sh and the mirror's .venv symlink assume one node, one checkout and one job -- four defects that only appear with simultaneous multi-node work

body:
The venv's editable install points at a **different checkout** from the one an agent edits.

`.venv.lustre/lib/python3.11/site-packages/lsms_library.pth` (and therefore `.venv.sqfs`, which is imaged from it) contains one line:

```
/global/scratch/fsa/fc_jevons/ligon/mirrors/LSMS_Library
```

That is the shared mirror — the same inode as `~/mirrors/LSMS_Library` (`~/mirrors` -> `var/mirrors` -> scratch), which is `origin` for every sucoder local-disk clone. `receive.denyCurrentBranch=updateInstead` holds its working tree at HEAD. Under tiering the working clone is `/local/job<ID>/mirrors/LSMS_Library`, a different path, holding committed **plus uncommitted** work.

## Measured, not reasoned

n0035.savio4, `.venv.sqfs` of 2026-09-07 mounted at `/local/job39123514/venv_img`, clone at `/local/job39123514/mirrors/LSMS_Library`:

| invocation | cwd | `PYTHONPATH` | imports |
|---|---|---|---|
| `python -c "import lsms_library"` | clone | unset | **clone** (`sys.path[0]` is `''` = cwd) |
| `python bench/x.py` | clone | unset | **MIRROR** — the trap |
| `python -m pytest tests/...` | clone | unset | **clone** |
| `python -c "import lsms_library"` | mirror | `=clone` | **MIRROR** — cwd beats `PYTHONPATH` |
| `python <clone>/bench/x.py` | mirror | `=clone` | clone |
| `python bench/x.py` | clone | `=clone` | **clone** — the lever works |

So the exposure is narrower than "everything imports the mirror", and it is worth stating precisely: **`python <script>.py` is the trap**, because Python sets `sys.path[0]` to the *script's own directory*, so cwd never enters `sys.path` and the `.pth` wins. `pytest` and `python -c` from the clone are accidentally correct.

This is the mechanism `CLAUDE.md`'s scrum-master addendum 3 already documents. What changed is the **consequence**. It used to be "main checkout vs. worktree". Under tiering it is "your last commit vs. your working tree", and on a node working a feature branch it is "`development` vs. your branch" — because the mirror's tree is on `development` whatever you pushed.

What runs as `python <script>.py`: every wave script, every `make` recipe that invokes one, `bench/feature_audit/scan.py`. The write side is GH #803 — a wave script whose imported package is the mirror is not under that package's `countries_root()`, so `to_parquet` drops the parquet next to the script, in a gitignored, ephemeral `/local` clone.

## Second defect from the same artifact: `__version__` is wrong everywhere

The master also carries `lsms_library-0.6.1.post138.dev0+02074edb.dist-info`, frozen at install time. `lsms_library/__init__.py:123-129` reads `__version__` from `importlib.metadata`, so:

```
code imported from : /local/job39123514/mirrors/LSMS_Library/lsms_library/__init__.py   (the clone)
__version__        : 0.6.1.post138.dev0+02074edb
```

`02074edb` is 2026-04-12, **2060 commits** before HEAD (`v0.14.0-70-gf27a82e2b`). Every session reports it. Under multi-node, "which code produced this?" has the same fixed wrong answer on every node.

## Proposal

Strip the editable install from the master before imaging, so the image is the dependency closure and nothing else, and make `PYTHONPATH=<clone>` the per-clone lever.

The argument for removing rather than overriding: with the `.pth` present, forgetting the lever gives a **silent wrong answer**; without it you get `ModuleNotFoundError`. That trade improves the more parallel the work is, because the silent mode means N agents confidently testing each other's committed code.

Decision needed — `.pth` only, or `pip uninstall lsms_library`:

- `.pth` only: fixes the import; the dist-info stays and `__version__` keeps lying.
- uninstall: removes both; `__version__` falls back to `"0.0.0"` (`__init__.py:129`, so nothing crashes) — uninformative rather than wrong. Cost: `.venv/bin/lsms-library` needs `PYTHONPATH` set, which the bootstrap does anyway.

**This needs a regression guard or it lasts until the next dependency bump.** `poetry install` installs the root project editable by default, and `SkunkWorks/savio_venv.md` explicitly recommends `poetry install` into the master. So: document `poetry install --no-root`, *and* make `bin/savio_venv.sh cmd_update` refuse to image a master that still contains `lsms_library.pth` or `lsms_library-*.dist-info`. The import sanity checks at `savio_venv.sh:34` and `:74` then need `PYTHONPATH` set.

Residual, which the fix does not close: cwd still beats `PYTHONPATH` for `python -c`, so the identity assert stays necessary. It should compare `realpath(lsms_library.__file__)` against `realpath(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)` — **not** against a `/local/job` prefix, which a legitimate burst job on scratch would fail, and not against a substring like `mirrors/LSMS_Library`, which matches both paths.

Related: #803 (write side), #948 (the same family, from the config side), `CLAUDE.md` scrum-master addendum 3.
title: The venv image's editable install names the shared mirror, so `python <script>.py` from a /local clone silently runs the mirror's code -- and `__version__` is 2060 commits stale

`reduce_to_agreed` (`lsms_library/build_transforms.py:422`) is the sanctioned explicit reducer for a table whose declared grain is coarser than its source (#323: "shared explicit-reducer helpers, country-invoked, fail-loud"). With `on_conflict='na'` it blanks a disagreeing cell and calls `warnings.warn()`. That is the whole disclosure. It files no grain report, and nothing stamps `lsms_grain_audit` into the parquet, so:

- the warning fires only on the cold build that ran the reducer; every warm read of the same parquet is silent;
- `grain_reports()` returns nothing for it, and `bench/feature_audit/scan.py` cannot drain what was never filed;
- the coverage grader (a cold build) may see the warning once; nobody reading the served table ever does.

That is exactly the failure #323 fixed for the core collapse ("the signal survives the cache -- this is the load-bearing part": `_audit_index_collapse` stamps the audit at write time and replays it on every warm read). The explicit reducer sits outside that machinery.

Measured on Uganda `crop_production` (branch for #824, red-team `slurm_logs/2026-09-09_epar_curation/REDTEAM_P2_824_uganda.org` item 7): 11 `(t, i, plot, j, u, condition, season)` groups disagree on `Unit_sold` and are blanked; a warm read produces 0 warnings; `grain_reports()` is empty; no Uganda parquet carries `lsms_grain_audit`. Callers today: `Uganda/_/uganda.py` (crop_production) and `build_transforms.py` itself (`collapse_to_cluster_grain`, i.e. every `cluster_features` built through it), so the gap covers both.

## What a fix would touch
- `reduce_to_agreed`: file a report through the same `country._audit_index_collapse` / grain-report path the core collapse uses (country, table, wave, the conflicting keys and columns, the count), so it is stamped into the parquet at write time and replayed warm; honour `LSMS_GRAIN_STRICT` through the same `_grain_strict()` predicate (one lever, one behaviour).
- A test that builds a conflicting fixture through `reduce_to_agreed(on_conflict='na')`, writes and re-reads the parquet, and asserts the report replays.

## What it must NOT do
- Not add an allowlist of known conflicting cells (same rule as `_grain_strict`).
- Not change what the reducer returns; the fix is disclosure, not behaviour.

Related: the same red-team found 433 Uganda `crop_production` groups already summing across distinct records on `development` (a missing level, most likely the 2018-19 AGSEC5B condition-2 slot of #848); that is a data question, separate from this disclosure gap.
title: reduce_to_agreed (build_transforms.py:422) only warnings.warn()s on a conflict: no grain report, no lsms_grain_audit stamp, so a warm read is silent and grain_reports() is empty

body:
Split out of the GH #863 red-team pass (`slurm_logs/2026-09-09_epar_curation/REDTEAM_P2_863_transforms.org` item 4). The *label-matching* half of that finding is fixed on `feat/863-transforms` (`_normalise_input_label`, commit `01b81d4c`): `nitrogen_kg` now resolves `Urea Fertilizer` -> `urea`, which moved Malawi from 331 plots / **0 kg N** to 33,113 plots / **835,012 kg N**. This issue is the half that is a *content* decision and was deliberately left alone.

## The gap

`_NITROGEN_CONTENT` (`lsms_library/transformations.py`) carries a nutrient-class vocabulary plus eight product names. Measured over the 11 warm `plot_inputs` tables (2026-09-09), these fertilizer-labelled inputs resolve to **no share at all** and therefore contribute nothing to `nitrogen_kg` / `fertilizer_rate`:

| label | country | rows | note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NPS` | Ethiopia | 5,264 | a real nitrogen fertilizer (nominally ~19% N); not in the map |
| `Manure` / `Compost` / `Other Organic` | Ethiopia | 27,261 / 4,295 / 2,651 | organic |
| `Organic Fertilizer` | Malawi, Tanzania | 11,075 / 727 | organic |
| `D Compound Fertilizer` | Malawi | 726 | a real Malawi blend; not in the map |
| `Organic manure` / `Organic compost` | Benin, Burkina Faso, CotedIvoire, Niger, Senegal, Togo | ~13,000 combined | organic |
| `Manure` / `Compost` / `Other organic` | Mali | 11,148 / 2,673 / 1,189 | organic |
| every label | Guinea-Bissau | 5,534 | Portuguese vocabulary; `Adubos inorgânicos - ureia` (190 rows) is real urea. `nitrogen_kg(Guinea-Bissau)` returns **0 rows** |

They are now *visible*: `nitrogen_kg` stamps `attrs['nitrogen_input_match']` (matched/unmatched rows and labels, the twin of `harvest_kg_factors`'s `shipped_matched`) and raises `NutrientCoverageWarning` naming the fertilizer-shaped labels that got no share. Visible is not fixed.

## Why it was not fixed in that PR

Each entry is an assertion about a nutrient content, not a spelling:

- **NPS** and **D Compound** need a sourced nominal N share, on the same footing as the map's existing citations (urea 46%, DAP 18%, NPK 17-17-17). Guessing one would be the thing `harvest_kg`'s "reported, never constructed" rule exists to prevent.
- **Organic inputs** are the harder call. Manure and compost *do* carry nitrogen (~0.5%, highly variable by source and moisture), so `0.0` is as much an invented number as any other. The alternative -- leaving them unmatched and loud -- at least does not put a fabricated figure into a published total. Whichever way it goes, it should be decided once and written down, not left to the accident of which labels happen to be keys.
- **Guinea-Bissau** needs its Portuguese vocabulary mapped (or a country-side harmonisation onto the canonical `input` labels), which is a config question, not a transform one.

## Suggested shape

1. Decide the organic policy explicitly (a sourced nominal share, or a documented refusal) and record it in `_NITROGEN_CONTENT`'s comment with its citation, as the inorganic entries already are.
2. Add `nps` and `d compound` with sourced shares.
3. Harmonise Guinea-Bissau's `input` labels country-side, or add its spellings.
4. Until then, the `NutrientCoverageWarning` is the work queue -- do not silence it with a 0.0 that asserts something nobody checked.

Callers can already override per-country today: `nitrogen_kg(plot_inputs, nitrogen_content={...})`.
title: _NITROGEN_CONTENT has no entry for NPS, D Compound or any organic input, so those fertilizer rows contribute 0 kg N silently

The Uganda 2009-10 harvest sentinel (#861, `99999`) has a sibling in Niger. Niger 2011-12 `crop_production` carries eleven rows of `Mil` (millet) with `Quantity == 999999` and `u == 'Unknown'`, surfaced by the #857 plausibility screen on the warm cache (ratio to the wave's reference x14,285.7; rung `t`, because the `(t, u, j)` and `(t, u)` cells for `Unknown` do not clear the 30-row floor).

## Evidence
- `slurm_logs/2026-09-09_epar_curation/REDTEAM_P1_quantity_screen.org` (Concern A): the all-warm-country sweep of the #857 screen lists "eleven `Mil 999,999 u=Unknown` rows in 2011-12" among Niger's 28 firings.
- `Niger/_/CONTENTS.org` documents the `u='Unknown'` sentinel for a quantity with no unit (#842/#847, "The `u` sentinel" section from ~:506) but does not mention a `999999` VALUE sentinel; grep for `999999` / `99999` there returns nothing.
- Not yet checked: whether the eleven rows are `999999` in the raw `.dta` (a Stata missing-value code) or produced by a unit-factor multiplication, and whether the same code occurs in `Quantity_sold` / `Value_sold` or in other Niger waves.

## What a fix would touch
- The raw column first: confirm the value in the source file and its label (a `.dta` value label or a `999999` = "ne sait pas" convention in the ECVMA questionnaire).
- If a sentinel: an exact-value map to missing at the wave level, the pattern #861 used (`qty_sentinel` in the wave colmap; `harvest_kg`/`crop_production_for_wave` strips the literal value only), a before/after count, and a `CONTENTS.org` entry beside the `u` sentinel section.
- Sweep the other Niger waves and the sold/value columns for `999999` / `9999` before declaring it 2011-12-only.

## What it must NOT do
- Never strip a range; the literal value only.
- Never clip or NaN the row on the strength of the plausibility screen alone -- the screen reports, and this issue exists to adjudicate what it reported.
- Never conflate with the `u='Unknown'` sentinel, which is a different fact (no unit recorded) and stays.

EPAR's Uganda, Tanzania and Ethiopia do-files each build a person-grain
"who decided what to farm on this plot" intermediate, then collapse it
away into a single plot-season gender categorical before the final
tables are saved. All twenty-one of the raw decision-maker variables
that intermediate is built from are completely unwired in this repo, and
the source files that carry them are already open in our own wave
scripts for other columns -- this is a column-add, not a new
acquisition, for three countries. But the repo has already reserved a
table name and a filing rule for exactly this construct
(`data_info.yml:228-232`, `plot_cultivation`), and any implementation
must use that grain, not a narrower one that omits `season`.

## What is wrong or missing

- Zero wiring today. `grep -rIni` across the whole of `lsms_library/` for
  every raw variable name below returns zero hits, each.
- The natural grain for "who farmed this plot this season" is `(t, i,
  plot, season, pid, role)`. A grain that drops `season` -- as an
  unqualified `(t, i, plot, pid, role)` proposal would -- collides
  Uganda's two seasons and Tanzania's two seasons onto one row and lets
  `_normalize_dataframe_index`'s `groupby().first()` silently discard the
  second season's decision-makers. That is the CLAUDE.md failure mode
  verbatim: "Duplicates on a declared index mean the IDENTIFIER IS BROKEN
  or a LEVEL IS MISSING."

## Evidence

**Ours -- the reservation already in the repo**
- `lsms_library/data_info.yml:228-232` -- the comment under `plot_features:`
  (`:227`): "Lasting
  plot/parcel characteristics (GH #167). Per-season detail (which crop,
  who farmed it this season, season-specific inputs, crop-share %)
  belongs in a future `plot_cultivation` table. See
  `slurm_logs/DESIGN_erhs_plot_features_2026-05-20.org` for the design
  rationale; Uganda is the Phase-1 pilot."
- `slurm_logs/DESIGN_erhs_plot_features_2026-05-20.org:54-57` -- "If
  someone later wants a per-plot, per-season `plot_cultivation` table
  (one row per `(t, v, i, plot_id, crop_seq)`, recording what was
  planted), that's a separate canonical-schema proposal -- file a new
  issue under #167's umbrella, do not retrofit `plot_features`."
- `crop_production`'s canonical grain already names `season`:
  `data_info.yml:577-578` writes it "(t, i, plot, j, u, condition, season)".
  But only two countries declare it as an index level today -- Uganda
  (`Uganda/_/data_scheme.yml`, `(t, i, plot, j, u, condition, season)`) and
  GhanaSPS. Ethiopia declares `(t, i, plot_id, j, u)` and Tanzania
  `(t, i, plot_id, j)`, so a `plot_cultivation` with a `season` level will
  NOT join those two countries' `crop_production` on season; that
  reconciliation is part of the proposal, not an assumption it can make.
- Ethiopia's `holder_id` is NOT a missing level despite first appearances:
  `lsms_library/countries/Ethiopia/_/ethiopia.py:747` and `:1000` already
  build `plot_id = format_id(holder_id)_format_id(parcel_id)_format_id(field_id)`
  (documented again at `:524`, `:849`, `:1181`), so Ethiopia's join key
  lines up as-is against `plot_features`/`crop_production`.

**Ours -- the three countries' source files already open**
- Uganda 2015-16: `lsms_library/countries/Uganda/2015-16/_/plot_labor.py:25-26`
  and `plot_inputs.py:22-23` already open `AGSEC3A.dta` / `AGSEC3B.dta` (the
  file carrying `a3aq3_3`, `a3aq3_4a`, `a3aq3_4b` and the season-B twins
  `a3bq3_3`, `a3bq3_4a`, `a3bq3_4b`); 2018-19, 2010-11, 2011-12, 2013-14
  use the same file/line shape.
- Ethiopia 2018-19: `lsms_library/countries/Ethiopia/2018-19/_/plot_inputs.py:28`,
  `plot_labor.py:21`, `plot_features.py:20` already open `sect3_pp_w4.dta`
  (the file carrying `s3q13`, `s3q15_1`, `s3q15_2`).
- Tanzania 2019-20/2020-21: `lsms_library/countries/Tanzania/2019-20/_/plot_inputs.py:21`,
  `plot_features.py:17`, `plot_labor.py:24` (and the 2020-21 equivalents
  `plot_inputs.py:17`, `plot_labor.py:21`, `plot_features.py:18`) already
  open `AG_SEC_3A.dta` / `ag_sec_3a.dta` (2020-21's file is **lowercase** --
  `2020-21/_/plot_labor.py:9-10` records the spelling already). That file
  carries `ag3a_08_1/_2/_3` in 2019-20 and the NPS W5/SDD spelling
  `ag3a_08b_1/_2/_3` in 2020-21 (plus the `ag3b_08_*`/`ag3b_08b_*` season-B
  fallbacks EPAR also reads). Tanzania 2012-13 is a new acquisition, not a
  column-add -- it lives in the `2008-15/` multi-round tree with no
  `AG_SEC_*` files at all.

**EPAR side** (commit `abfbdc9301242527b7543606aad1ad6eed2e6530`,
`LSMS-Agricultural-Indicators-Code/`)
- `Uganda UNPS/Uganda UNPS Wave 5/EPAR_UW_Uganda_UNPS_W5.do:413-424` --
  the saved person-grain intermediate `Uganda_NPS_W5_dm_ids.dta`, columns
  `(hhid, parcel_id, plot_id, season, id_no, pid, formal_land_rights,
  personid, female, age, hh_head)`.
- `EPAR_UW_Uganda_UNPS_W5.do:433-439` -- the collapse rule: `collapse
  (mean) female (firstnm) dm1_gender, by(hhid parcel_id plot_id season)`
  (`:433`), then thresholds (`:435-439`)
  (male-only / female-only / anything fractional is mixed / the head's
  sex where nothing matched). Uganda collapses by `(hhid, parcel_id,
  plot_id, season)` -- `season` is explicitly in the `by()` list, not
  optional.
- `Tanzania NPS/Tanzania NPS Wave 3/EPAR_UW_Tanzania_NPS_W3.do:261` (the
  saved intermediate `Tanzania_NPS_W3_plot_dm_ids.dta`) and `:263`
  (`collapse (mean) female (firstnm) dm1_gender, by(hhid plot_id season
  cultivated)`) -- Tanzania's twin, `season` likewise in the `by()` list.
- `Ethiopia ESS/Ethiopia ESS Wave 4/EPAR_UW_Ethiopia_ESS_W4.do:513-515` --
  Ethiopia's twin: `keep hhid holder_id parcel_id plot_id personid female`
  then the save. No role slot, and no `season` in the key -- the reshape at
  `:510` is `i(parcel_id plot_id hhid holder_id dummy)`. Whether an Ethiopia
  row should carry a null `season` or the level should be country-optional is
  part of what the proposal must settle.

## What a fix would touch

- A design proposal document, written against
  `DESIGN_lsms_plus_individual_disaggregation_2026-06-14.org` and
  `DESIGN_erhs_plot_features_2026-05-20.org`) for a `plot_cultivation`
  table at grain `(t, i, plot, season, pid, role)`, filed under #167's
  reserved name and #439's owner-expansion convention.
- Roles: decision-maker slots 1-3 (Uganda has two decision-maker slots
  for some sections, per `a3aq3_3`/`a3aq3_4a`/`a3aq3_4b`), with the
  head-of-household fallback documented as a **transform rule** applied
  at read time (mirroring EPAR's mean-of-female-then-threshold logic),
  never as a stored row -- the raw per-slot rows are what gets stored.
- Column-adds in the three wave scripts named above, once the schema
  proposal is accepted; then the other waves of each country.
- Reconciliation with `crop_production`'s `season` level where it exists
  (Uganda, GhanaSPS) and a stated rule for the countries where it does not
  (Ethiopia, Tanzania), plus Ethiopia's `holder_id` fold-in (already handled,
  no extra work needed there).

## What it must NOT do

- Never propose or accept a grain that omits `season` -- both Uganda and
  Tanzania collapse by season in the source pipeline; dropping it here
  reproduces the exact grain-collapse bug class CLAUDE.md documents.
- Never retrofit `plot_features` with this detail -- the design doc
  (`DESIGN_erhs_plot_features_2026-05-20.org:54-57`) already rules that
  out explicitly.
- Never store the head-of-household fallback value as if it were a
  reported row -- it is a derived/transform result and must be
  computable, not baked into the parquet.
- Never assume Ethiopia needs a `holder_id`-to-`plot_id` reconciliation
  step -- it doesn't; the existing fold-in already produces the matching
  key.

## Cross-references

Filed under #167 (plot_features, closed) and #439 (LSMS+
individual-disaggregation, open) per both issues' own filing
instructions. Companion Phase-3 items (not this issue): a `dm_gender`
transform reducing over this new table, and a separate `individual_assets
(t, i, j, pid)` feature from Ethiopia `sect11_hh_w4` / Uganda `AGSEC2A`,
`AGSEC6A`, `gsec14` -- #439's flagship, built from data we already hold. The
transforms-umbrella issue filed alongside this one carries the rest of the
Phase-3 transform list.

Source: slurm_logs/2026-09-09_epar_curation/LEARNINGS.org (L4)
title: Schema proposal: plot_cultivation, a per-season plot decision-maker table (#167's reserved name, #439's convention)

Uganda 2018-19 AGSEC5B carries a SECOND harvest record per plot-crop -- `s5bq06a_2` (quantity), `s5bq06b_2` (unit), `s5bq06c_2` (condition), `s5bq06d_2` (kg factor), plus its own months and decision-maker columns -- populated on ~20% of rows (1,435 of 7,041). `CROP_COLMAPS['2018-19']['B']['conditions']` wires slot 1 only, so those records are not served.

What the slot IS, settled by the #842 Uganda agent (`slurm_logs/...`, `Uganda/_/CONTENTS.org`): the old caution that it "may be a SEASON slot" is wrong -- its harvest-end dates are June/July 2018 on 1,423 of 1,435 rows, the same window as slot 1, while AGSEC5A (the genuine 2017 second season) ends November/December 2017. It is a second **condition** slot: the same plot-crop harvested in a second state (e.g. fresh and dry), exactly the structure `crop_production`'s `condition` index level exists to carry (GH #323/#637: "the same plot-crop-season carries one record PER CONDITION"). Note the mixed naming vintages inside one file: slot 1 uses legacy `a5bq6{b,c,d}`, slot 2 uses WB `s5bq06{b,c,d}_2`.

Why it was not wired in #842: adding it changes the served row count (+~1,435), and that fix was verified on a "rows identical" invariant. It needs its own before/after: rows added, `condition` values on the new rows, duplicate-index check against slot 1 (a slot-2 record with the SAME condition as slot 1 would collide on `(t, i, plot, j, u, condition, season)` and be summed by the additive collapse -- measure whether any do), `harvest_kg` sum before/after, and the `KgFactor` column carried from `s5bq06d_2`.

Also check 2019-20, whose WB-named columns come "one pair per slot" (`s5{a,b}q06b_{1,2}`), for the same unwired second slot.

## The defect

`food_prices(units='unitprice')` is documented as serving the price the survey
recorded. `lsms_library/transformations.py:1368-1372`:

> ``'unitprice'``: reported ``Price`` (currency / native u).
> NaN where **the survey did not record a unit price**.  This mode reflects the
> canonical ``food_acquired.Price`` column — **market price** for ``s='purchased'``,
> **farmgate** for ``s='produced'``, imputed for ``s='inkind'``.

For Uganda that is not what the column holds. UBOS's "Market Price" columns are
**back-calculated `Expenditure / Quantity`**, not independently elicited prices,
so `units='unitprice'` and `units='unitvalue'` return the same number on 94.4-99.9%
of rows -- and a user who reads the docstring will treat them as two independent
sources and get a spurious agreement.

(Note on wording: `slurm_logs/price_sources/Uganda/REPORT.org` D5 paraphrases the
docstring as documenting `unitprice` as *"the survey's own price question"*. The
literal text is quoted above; the paraphrase is fair but is not a verbatim quote,
so the exact string is given here instead.)

## Instances

| country | wave(s) | table | count | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Uganda | all eight | `food_acquired.Price` / `food_prices(units='unitprice')` | share of purchased rows whose reported "Market Price" differs from `Expenditure/Quantity` by more than 1e-6, by wave: **1.72 / 5.62 / 1.09 / 5.21 / 1.51 / 0.06 / 0.08 / 0.09 %** (2005-06 … 2019-20), n = 24,697–35,982 per wave. Median log ratio **0.0** in every wave; pooled median gap 0.000, IQR 0.000, over 4,686 cells | `slurm_logs/price_sources/Uganda/REPORT.org` §2. **Re-verified on the raw `.dta` before the library touches anything**: `h15bq12` against `(h15bq5+h15bq7)/(h15bq4+h15bq6)` gives 1.72% / 5.21% / 1.51% differing in 2005-06 / 2011-12 / 2013-14, and the same holds for the farmgate pair (`Value_own/Qty_own`: 1.36% / 4.75% / 1.01%). The residual few percent is **not** the home/away purchase-leg fold -- among differing rows, only 0.8% / 0.4% / 0.2% have both legs populated |

## Why it matters

This is a documentation defect with a measurable analytic consequence. The whole
point of separating `unitprice` from `unitvalue` is that one is elicited and the
other is derived, so an analyst can check them against each other. For Uganda they
are the same quantity wearing two names: any comparison of the two "sources" for
Uganda returns a median log gap of exactly 0.000 and looks like a triumphant
validation, when it is an identity. The price comparison had to **drop source 2 for
Uganda entirely** on the strength of the raw-file check above.

The docstring is not wrong in general -- for countries that do elicit a price it
describes the column correctly. It is wrong in that it offers no way to tell which
kind of country you are holding, and it currently reads as a guarantee.

## Proposed fix

A docs change in library code, plus optionally one cheap diagnostic:

1. Amend the `units=` docstring in `transformations.py` to say that
   `food_acquired.Price` is **whatever the country's source recorded**, which in
   some countries (Uganda measured; check the other `Price`-bearing countries) is
   the statistical office's own `Expenditure / Quantity` rather than an elicited
   price -- so `'unitprice'` and `'unitvalue'` are not guaranteed independent.
2. Record the distinction per country where it is known, next to the `Price`
   column's provenance in `CONTENTS.org`. Uganda's is documented in
   `slurm_logs/price_sources/Uganda/REPORT.org` §2.
3. Optionally, a one-line diagnostic: if `unitprice` and `unitvalue` agree on
   >90% of a country's rows, the column is derived, and saying so once at read
   time would save every future user this measurement.

Related: #828 (`units='unitprice'` returns an empty frame **silently** where a
country has no `Price` at all -- 6 countries). That issue is the "no price" case;
this one is the "a price that is not a price" case.

Surfaced by the five-source price comparison, 2026-09-08; per-country evidence in `slurm_logs/price_sources/Uganda/REPORT.org`; pattern `P05-price-absent` in `slurm_logs/price_sources/DATA_PROBLEMS.csv`.
title: food_prices(units='unitprice') docs: for Uganda the stored Price IS Exp/Qty, not an elicited price (94.4-99.9% of rows)

## The pattern

The community price questionnaire prices a **(product, variety)** pair -- "maize,
white, sold in a 100 kg sack" is a different observation from "maize, white, sold
by the tia". The canonical `community_prices` grain is `(t, v, j, u)`, with no
variety level, so in three countries the build keeps **one row per key, chosen by
row order**, and the rest are dropped. The choice is not recorded, not stated in a
docstring, and not reproducible from the delivered table: a user cannot tell which
variety's price they are holding, or that there were others.

## Instances

| country | wave(s) | table | count | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mali | 2014-15 | `community_prices` | **7,263 of 32,479 (22.4%)** of `(v, j, u)` groups had more than one priced variety | `lsms_library/countries/Mali/_/mali.py:849-852`; the dropped axis is `s04q02` (questionnaire §4.04) in `EACIS04_p2.dta`. Concentré de tomate prices three varieties under `u='Boîte'` at **600 / 125 / 225 FCFA**; Cube alimentaire is 25 FCFA per "Unité" in one variety and 1,300 FCFA per "Paquet" in another |
| Tanzania | 2019-20, 2020-21 | `community_prices` | **243 of 261 groups (2019-20)** and **1,149 of 1,281 (2020-21)** -- about 90% | `tanzania.community_prices_for_wave`, which carries its own GH #637 comment. The `j` label deliberately lumps e.g. millet and sorghum, and the two source codes carry different prices, so the keep-first is resolving genuine disagreement |
| Niger | 2011-12, 2014-15 | `community_prices` | **90 variety codes collapsed onto 45 products** | `cs07q02` / `cs07q02l` in both raw files -- e.g. "mais blanc vendu en sac de 100 kg" and "mais blanc vendu au tia" are distinct varieties of one product |

## Why it matters

A cluster-item price is the whole point of `community_prices`: it is the only
source in the price comparison that is a *market* price rather than a household's
back-calculated unit value, and it is the yardstick every farmgate margin is
measured against. Mali's tomato-paste spread (600 vs 125 FCFA for the same
`(v, j, u)`) is a 4.8x range decided by row order. Because one row survives and it
is well-formed, nothing downstream can detect that a choice was made -- the grain
audit is silent (this is a wave-script collapse, not a core one), and the cell
grades `sane`.

Note that the Niger and Mali cases are compounded by the variety often encoding
the **unit basis** ("vendu en sac de 100 kg"), so dropping variety can drop the
only record of what the price is per.

## Proposed fix

This one needs a maintainer decision, not a patch, and the two candidate answers
pull in different directions:

1. **Add `variety` to the index.** Faithful to the instrument, and it makes the
   `(t, v, j, u, variety)` grain unique so no choice is made. Cost: it changes the
   shape `community_prices()` serves in three countries, and consumers joining on
   `(t, v, j, u)` get a fan-out.
2. **Select on a stated rule** -- modal variety, or largest n -- rather than row
   order, and document it in the docstring. Cheaper, but note that Tanzania's own
   code comment cites #323 D1 ("duplicates on a declared index mean the identifier
   is broken or a level is missing -- fix the index; do not declare a reducer"),
   which argues against this branch.

GhanaLSS already demonstrates a third shape: it carries an `obs` level so the
multiple readings survive. Whichever is chosen, the current state -- an
undocumented row-order selection over a fifth to nine-tenths of the groups -- is
the one option that should not persist.

Surfaced by the five-source price comparison, 2026-09-08; per-country evidence in `slurm_logs/price_sources/<Country>/REPORT.org`; pattern `P03-variety-collapse` in `slurm_logs/price_sources/DATA_PROBLEMS.csv`.
title: community_prices drops the variety axis, keeping one (t,v,j,u) row arbitrarily (Mali 22.4%, Tanzania ~90%, Niger 90->45)

body:
## The pattern

Two countries carry a claim in a config or documentation file that the data
contradict. CLAUDE.md is unambiguous about why this class matters -- *"Never write
an unevidenced 'no module here' claim, in a verdict file or in a YAML comment"* --
because such a claim is unfalsifiable in practice (nothing records how it was
reached) and it **suppresses work**: the next person reads it and does not check.
Both instances below did exactly that during this sweep.

## Instances

| country | wave(s) | file | count | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mali | 2014-15 | `Mali/_/data_scheme.yml`, the `food_acquired:` comment | **3 false claims** | the comment asserts the wave "incorrectly maps `Quantity: s13q02`", that it "continues to emit a legacy non-canonical shape", and that runtime output "mixes shapes across waves". All three have been false since GH #380; all three Mali waves were verified to return `(t, v, i, j, u, s)`. `Mali/_/data_scheme.yml` vs `Mali/2014-15/_/mapping.py` |
| Tanzania | 2019-20, 2020-21 | `Tanzania/_/CONTENTS.org` (and closed issue #112) | `hh_j03_2` non-null on **12,825 / 4,699** rows | `CONTENTS.org` says the quantity columns are MISSING and marks it "Critical -- blocks food_prices". They are all **present**; the World Bank re-released the files. `get_dataframe('Tanzania/2019-20/Data/HH_SEC_J1.dta')`. #112 is already closed, but the `CONTENTS.org` entry that made the claim is still live -- exactly the "a CLOSED issue can still have a live caveat parked there" case CLAUDE.md warns dispatchers about. Corrected on an unpushed worktree branch as `38e988ee` |

A third, adjacent instance is filed separately as part of the label-fold issue:
`Malawi/_/data_scheme.yml` claims the `crop_production` crop labels "JOIN
food_acquired.j", and **17 of 41 do not**.

## Why it matters

Mali's comment cost this sweep a re-check of a shape that had been canonical for
months. Tanzania's cost more: it says the country's food quantities are missing
and marks it Critical, so the honest reading is "Tanzania cannot take part in a
price study" -- and the quantities are there. The general failure mode is the one
CLAUDE.md records for Albania, where a `data_scheme.yml` comment asserting "earlier
waves have no shocks module" was false and suppressed roughly five cells of work
with nothing recorded about how the claim had been reached.

## Proposed fix

- **Tanzania** -- correct the `CONTENTS.org` entry (done in `38e988ee`, unpushed)
  and decide whether #113 is still wanted now that #112's premise is gone.
- **Mali** -- correct the `data_scheme.yml` comment. **Not done, deliberately, and
  the reason is itself worth an issue**: it was measured that appending a comment to
  `data_scheme.yml` moves **all five** probed Mali table cache hashes, while the same
  edit to `CONTENTS.org` moves **none**. `Country._table_cache_hash` hashes
  `data_scheme.yml` by name, so a pure-comment edit cold-rebuilds every table in the
  country. The correction was therefore made in `Mali/_/CONTENTS.org` instead
  (`ad5119e3`, unpushed) and flagged for whoever next edits `data_scheme.yml` for a
  substantive reason.

  That side-effect is a framework smell in its own right: **there is currently no
  way to fix a false comment in a `data_scheme.yml` without paying a corpus rebuild
  for the country**, which is a standing incentive to leave false claims in place.
  Hashing the parsed YAML rather than the file bytes would remove it.

Surfaced by the five-source price comparison, 2026-09-08; per-country evidence in `slurm_logs/price_sources/<Country>/REPORT.org`; pattern `P16-false-config-claim` in `slurm_logs/price_sources/DATA_PROBLEMS.csv`.
title: A config comment the data contradict: Mali data_scheme.yml (3 false claims since #380) and Tanzania CONTENTS.org (#112)

## The pattern

#323 is closed, but what it landed was an **audit** of the two grain-collapse
sites, not a repair of the keys that trip them. Three countries still hand
`_collapse_to_cluster_grain` / `_normalize_dataframe_index` a `(t, v)` key that is
not unique, so on every build the cluster-grain projection destroys disagreeing
rows and `groupby().first()` assembles a composite cluster from whichever
household answered first. The `GrainCollapseWarning` fires -- loudly, correctly,
and on every build -- and then the wrong value is served anyway, because a warning
is not a fix. In each case the root cause is the one CLAUDE.md names: **the
identifier is broken or a level is missing**, not that a reducer is needed.

#819 covers a different half of this (the `_v_to_str` leading-zero strip and the
v-join running before `id_walk`). These are the instances #819 does not touch.

## Instances

| country | wave(s) | table | count | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ethiopia | all but 2018-19 | `cluster_features` | **373 / 454 / 732 / 1,240 rows** destroyed (34 / 43 / 72 / 111 conflicting tuples) | `GrainCollapseWarning` raised on every build in this run. The `(t, v)` key is not unique because `v` is the bare cluster code |
| Ethiopia | all | `cluster_features` | **30 of 37** distinct `District` codes occur in more than one `Region` (max 11), and the formatting drifts: `'1'` in W1-W3, `'01'` in W4-W5 | `District` is a bare 1-2 digit code that is not a district identity. This is the *cause* on the Ethiopia side -- a `v` built from it cannot be unique. `slurm_logs/price_sources/Ethiopia/analysis.py:_prep`; worked around there with a `Region\|District` composite (53 orphan rows nulled so they cannot form a phantom `nan\|nan` cell) |
| Tanzania | 5 of 6 waves | `cluster_features` | **605 / 1,304 / 404 / 197 / 177 rows** | `GrainCollapseWarning` raised in this run; `Tanzania/_/CONTENTS.org` §"The residue" already proposes the fix. A `District` label can be one household's answer rather than the cluster's |
| Uganda | 2013-14 through 2019-20 | `cluster_features` | `GrainConflictWarning` on **122-221 of 706-875 clusters per wave** (`Rural`, `Latitude`, `Longitude` blanked) | build-time warnings. Related to but distinct from #689 (Uganda `cluster_features` is at PARISH grain from 2013-14) -- #689 is about the grain being *coarser than the EA*; this is about the resulting key not being unique |

## Why it matters

The cluster is the bottom rung of every geography ladder in the price comparison,
and it is the rung at which a market price means anything. A destroyed row is not
merely lost: `groupby().first()` **skips NA per column**, so a conflicting group
collapses to a *composite* row assembled from the first non-null value of each
column independently -- a cluster that exists nowhere in the survey (this is #637's
mechanism, firing here). CLAUDE.md already records the sharpest measured instance
of the same class: Kazakhstan 1996 cluster `v=126` holds 178 Urban households and
2 Rural and `.first()` returns **`Rural`** for the whole cluster. Ethiopia's
`District` is worse in kind rather than in degree -- because 30 of 37 codes are
reused across Regions, `District` alone is not a geography at all, and any
analysis that groups on it silently pools households from up to 11 different
regions.

The signal is at least visible now (#323's audit is stamped into the parquet and
replayed on the warm read). What is missing is that nobody has fixed a key.

## Proposed fix

Per country, at the config/wave-script level -- **not** by declaring a reducer,
which `SkunkWorks/grain_aggregation_policy.org` §3a forbids and a test pins:

- **Ethiopia** -- make `v` a composite of district + cluster code, and make
  `District` a composite (or namespace it by `Region`) so it is an identity rather
  than a within-region serial. Fix the W3->W4 zero-padding drift at the same time.
- **Tanzania** -- the `harmonize_district` table already proposed in
  `Tanzania/_/CONTENTS.org` §"The residue".
- **Uganda** -- resolve alongside #689; the parish-grain question and the
  non-unique-key question have the same answer (a cluster key that is the sampling
  cluster).

Surfaced by the five-source price comparison, 2026-09-08; per-country evidence in `slurm_logs/price_sources/<Country>/REPORT.org`; pattern `P07-cluster-grain` in `slurm_logs/price_sources/DATA_PROBLEMS.csv`.

## The defect

`lsms_library/country.py:640` excludes `CONTENTS.org` from the `*.org` files
folded into the cache hash, with an explicit and correct rationale:

```python
# Build-input file suffixes ... We hash *all* ``*.org`` in the relevant ``_/``
# dir except the ones below, which are pure documentation never read by a
# build step -- hashing them would cause a spurious full-country rebuild on a
# docs edit.
_ORG_HASH_SKIP = {"CONTENTS.org"}
```

The premise is false for exactly one country. `Tanzania/_/food_acquired.py:34`
reads a live build table out of it:

```python
fl = df_from_orgfile('CONTENTS.org','food_labels')
```

So editing Tanzania's `food_labels` table changes what `food_acquired` is built
from and moves **no** cache hash. The stale parquet is served, indefinitely, and
`lsms-library cache clear` is the only way to notice.

## Instances

| country | wave(s) | table | count | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tanzania | all | `food_acquired` (country-level `_/food_acquired.py`) | 1 country -- and it is the only one; `grep -rn "'CONTENTS.org'" lsms_library/countries/*/_/*.py` was run over the whole corpus | `lsms_library/countries/Tanzania/_/food_acquired.py:34` vs `lsms_library/country.py:640` |

## Why it matters

This is the same class as #757 (a `categorical_mapping.org` edit invisible to
`Wave._input_hash`) and #790 (a gitignored generated `.csv` that *is* hashed): a
build input outside the fingerprint means a correct edit produces no rebuild, and
the library then re-stamps the stale output as fresh. It is worse than a plain
staleness bug because the exclusion is *deliberate and documented* -- the next
person to read `_ORG_HASH_SKIP` will conclude, correctly for 39 countries and
incorrectly for Tanzania, that `CONTENTS.org` is documentation.

## Proposed fix

Move `food_labels` out of `Tanzania/_/CONTENTS.org` and into `_/food_items.org`,
which **is** hashed. That keeps `_ORG_HASH_SKIP`'s premise true rather than
special-casing it, and leaves `CONTENTS.org` as the documentation file every other
country's tooling assumes it is.

Cost, stated: the move forces a corpus-wide rebuild of Tanzania `food_acquired`
(the hash changes by construction). Worth scheduling with the `new_harmonize_units`
truncation fix filed alongside this one, since that rebuilds the same table.

An alternative -- narrowing `_ORG_HASH_SKIP` to a per-country setting -- would
work but leaves the trap in place for the next script that reaches into
`CONTENTS.org`.

Surfaced by the five-source price comparison, 2026-09-08; per-country evidence in `slurm_logs/price_sources/Tanzania/REPORT.org`; pattern `P20-cache-hash-hole` in `slurm_logs/price_sources/DATA_PROBLEMS.csv`.
title: Tanzania/_/food_acquired.py reads a build table out of CONTENTS.org, which the cache hash deliberately skips

body:
## The pattern

A `harmonize_food` / `harmonize_crop` Preferred Label folds two commodities into
one `j`: the raw form and the processed form, the crop as harvested and the good
as consumed, a vendor snack and the raw nut. The fold is invisible downstream --
the label is a valid canonical string and the table builds -- but any price
comparison across the fold is measuring **processing, not marketing**. Five of
the eight countries in the price comparison carry at least one, and in four of
them the survey *records* the distinguishing state in a column the build does not
read.

## Instances

| country | wave(s) | table | count | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Malawi | all four | `crop_production` | the shelled/unshelled state is never read; `condition=` is a parameter `_harvest_block` accepts and whose name occurs nowhere in the function body | `ag_i02c` / `ag_g13c` in the source; `lsms_library/countries/Malawi/_/malawi.py:915` (`def _harvest_block(..., condition=None, ...)`). Consequence measured: `unit_value / crop sale` per-kg ratios of **3.08 (Rice, 33 cells)**, **2.90 (Finger Millet)**, **4.99 (Groundnut, 6 cells)**, and `community / crop sale` **2.86 (Rice, 30 cells)** -- milling and shelling yields are about 65% each, i.e. ~1.5x, and these are 2-3 of those stacked |
| Uganda | all | food `Aggregate` labels | Maize gap ratio **3.33x** on 36 cells (1-vs-4); the same fold hits Millet | the Aggregate label folds `Maize (grains)`, `Maize (cobs)` and `Maize (flour)` into one "Maize" while the crop side is grain (`dried_grain` on 2,109 rows); purchased unit values in 2013-14 are 1,000 UGX/kg for grain and 1,800 for flour. `Millet` vs `Millet Flour` is 2,000 vs 3,000 in 2018-19. Cassava looks clean at **1.17x** precisely because `Cassava` and `Cassava (flour)` happen to be *separate* Aggregate labels. `slurm_logs/price_sources/Uganda/REPORT.org` §5 (`three_way_by_item.csv`) |
| Uganda | all | `harmonize_crop` | 7,794 sale rows (**17%**) could not join the food axis | `Uganda/_/categorical_mapping.org` codes 141, 741 -- the `j` labels break the table's own stated join contract. Fix: 141 -> `Millet`, 741 -> `Matoke`. Fixed on an unpushed worktree branch as `179af546` |
| Tanzania | 2019-20, 2020-21 | `crop_production` `j` (`harmonize_crop`) | 4 labels of the 21 that join | four crop labels reuse a food label whose *processed* form is a different commodity: Coffee & Cocoa (cherry vs roasted) **15.2-16.0x** apart, Nuts (in-shell vs processed) **2.7-13.0x**, Seeds 0.84x, Tea (dry). `slurm_logs/price_sources/Tanzania/cells.csv`, national rung |
| Malawi | 2016-17, 2019-20 | `food_acquired` | 2 of 5 waves | `harmonize_food` maps Preferred Label `Groundnut` <- **`Boiled groundnuts`** (a vendor snack) while the raw nut has its own labels `Groundnut (Shelled)` / `Groundnut Dried (Unshelled)`. Its own Aggregate Label admits it: `Groundnut, Vendor/Boiled`. `Malawi/_/categorical_mapping.org:90` vs `:93`, `:144`. **This does not explain the 5.0x above** -- all 6 per-kg Groundnut cells come from 2010-11 and 2013-14, the waves in which `Groundnut` is the raw nut; checked, not assumed |
| Malawi | -- | `crop_production` / `community_prices` | **17 of 41** crop labels do not join | `Malawi/_/data_scheme.yml` claims they "JOIN food_acquired.j". `Maize` (crop) does not join `Maize Grain (Not As Ufa)`; `Beans` joins neither; `Macadamia` vs `Macademia Nuts` is a spelling |
| Niger | 2018-19, 2021-22 | `food_acquired` | 178 `j` labels of which ~8 are drift pairs; the undecoded code `166` is 468 rows | cross-wave label drift leaves near-duplicate items: `Chou`/`Choux`, `Aubergine,`/`Aubergine, Courge/Courgette`, `Sucre (poudre ou morceaux)`/`Sucre poudre`/`Sucre morceaux`. `food_acquired().j.unique()` |
| Ethiopia | all | `crop_production` vs the price tables | Leafy Greens ratio **0.40**, Banana **0.045** | a shared `u` label spans two physical quantities across the two sides (likely a bunch/heap sold at farmgate against a Kg retail price), producing *negative* marketing margins. `slurm_logs/price_sources/Ethiopia/by_item.csv`. Strictly a `u`-axis fold rather than a `j`-axis one; recorded here because the symptom and the diagnosis discipline are identical |

## Why it matters

This is what makes a measured "marketing margin" **wrong rather than merely
noisy**, and it is not a footnote: in the pooled synthesis it is the entire
difference between a `same_good` median ratio of **1.5000** on 458 cells and a
`processed` median of **3.0000** on 111 cells (`slurm_logs/price_sources/pooled_models.csv`).
A user who reads `Country('Malawi').food_prices()` against `crop_production` and
finds groundnut at 5.0x has no way to learn from the API that the farmer sold
unshelled nuts and the household bought shelled ones -- the survey asked, and the
library dropped the answer. Uganda's maize case is worse, because the fold happens
at the `Aggregate` label the `labels=` kwarg exists to serve: the flagship
cross-country aggregation silently averages grain against flour.

## Proposed fix

- **Carry the state the survey records.** Malawi: read `ag_i02c` / `ag_g13c` and
  give `crop_production` a `condition` level (the parameter is already in
  `_harvest_block`'s signature). Tanzania: distinguish harvest form from consumed
  form in `harmonize_crop` rather than reusing the food label.
- **Split the folded labels.** Malawi: `Boiled groundnuts` gets its own label, as
  `Boiled sweet potatoes` already did (`- Boiled (Vendor)`) -- the fold looks like a
  difflib artefact of the `food_items.org` construction. Uganda: keep
  `Maize (flour)` and `Millet Flour` out of the grain Aggregate, exactly as
  `Cassava (flour)` already is.
- **Repair the joins that are asserted and untrue.** Uganda `harmonize_crop`
  141 -> `Millet`, 741 -> `Matoke` (`179af546`). Malawi: a crop->food crosswalk, or
  withdraw `data_scheme.yml`'s "JOIN food_acquired.j" claim -- 17 of 41 labels do
  not (see the separate false-config-claim issue).
- **Niger**: extend `harmonize_food` over the drift pairs and decode `166`.
- **Ethiopia**: a per-item unit audit on the crop-vs-price pairs.

Note that the fix direction here is the **opposite** of the unit-vocabulary issue
filed alongside this one: there the answer is to fold two labels into one, here it
is to split one label into two. Do not let a single "harmonisation" pass do both.

Surfaced by the five-source price comparison, 2026-09-08; per-country evidence in `slurm_logs/price_sources/<Country>/REPORT.org`; pattern `P09-label-fold` in `slurm_logs/price_sources/DATA_PROBLEMS.csv`.
title: harmonize_* folds raw and processed into one `j` in 5 countries: Malawi groundnut 5.0x, Uganda maize 3.33x are milling

body:
## The pattern

The `u` axis is not one axis. Across 7 of the 8 countries in the five-source price
comparison, a single physical unit ships under two or more labels -- two Preferred
Labels for one bowl, a canonicalisation applied in one wave and not its siblings,
five spellings of "kilogram" *inside the shared `u` table*, the same unit
capitalised differently on two tables of the same country. Nothing warns: the
labels are all valid strings, the tables all build, and the grain audit is
correctly silent because no row is destroyed. The damage is that the rows never
meet -- a per-unit price on `food_acquired` and the same per-unit price on
`community_prices` or `crop_production` sit in different cells and simply fail to
match.

## Instances

| country | wave(s) | table | count | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GhanaLSS | 1991-92, 1998-99, 2005-06, 2012-13 | `food_acquired` | **473,660 produced rows** (93,577 + 33,153 + 149,023 + 197,907); 100% of produced rows in 2005-06 and 2012-13 | a **regression**: `git show c345d317:...GhanaLSS/_/food_acquired.py` line 52 applies the `_/unit_labels.org` Preferred-Label map; commit `6de0ce37` ("wire GhanaLSS food_acquired end-to-end (Phase 2)") dropped it and only 2016-17's wave script re-implemented it. `unit_labels.org` already contains every mapping the four waves need (8/9, 8/9, 29/30, 40/41 of their off-axis labels). Fixed on an unpushed worktree branch as `359e52af`, verified cold: shape 5,259,320x3 unchanged, all 14 `(t,s)` cell counts identical, off-axis `u` rows 93,577/33,153/149,023/197,907 -> **0/0/0/0** |
| Niger | 2011-12, 2014-15, 2018-19 | `_/categorical_mapping.org` (`u`) | 18,759 `food_acquired` + 4,167 crop rows (2018-19); 825 + 3,196 (2011-12); 112 + 3,307 (2014-15) | `Tia` and `Tiya` carried **two Preferred Labels for one unit**, so no price per bowl could ever match across tables. Six instrument label sets each carry exactly ONE tia-like entry (`as02eq07b` 5='tiya', `AS02EQ07B` 5='Tiya', `s16Cq12b` 8='Tia', `s16cq16b` 3='Tiya', `s07Bq03b` 512='Tiya', `cs07q03/q05` 3='tia'); 2018-19's own food and crop modules disagree with each other. Fixed on an unpushed worktree branch as `4732a5eb` |
| Malawi | all five | `food_acquired` | 640 distinct `u` labels; 2004-05 alone has 35,805 `Kg` rows | `Malawi/_/categorical_mapping.org` `u` codes 07 vs 07a/07b: `Kg` / `kg` / `Kgs` / `Kilogram` / `Kkilogram` for one unit, and `No.12 Plate` vs `No 12 Plate` are two spellings *inside the shared table* |
| Tanzania | 2019-20, 2020-21 | `food_acquired` vs `community_prices` | 288 + 310 source-1 rows; 442 + 2,423 source-5 rows | the same unit is spelled `piece` on one table and `Piece` on the other, so a native-unit join silently drops every Piece comparison. See "What must NOT be folded" below -- the config forbids the obvious fix, with a reason |
| Mali | 2018-19, 2021-22 vs 2014-15 | `food_acquired` | 5,682 (`Boîte`) vs 7,799 + 5,854 (`Boite`) | `slurm_logs/price_sources/Mali/analysis.py` PRE-CHECK (i). Harmless within a wave; it would silently split a cross-wave unit panel |
| Ethiopia | all | all three price tables | 1,944 + 77 + 654 rows dropped from sources 1 / 4 / 5 | `u = "Other(Specify)"` vs `"Other (Specify)"` -- the spacing differs *across tables of the same country* (`slurm_logs/price_sources/Ethiopia/analysis.py:JUNK_UNITS`) |
| Ethiopia | all | `crop_production` | 550 of 85,519 rows (0 of the 3,721 usable sold rows) | mojibake fragments the axis: `"Zorba/Akara Ï¿½ Large"` alongside `"Zorba/Akara Large"`. `Ethiopia/_/ethiopia.py` `_clean_unit_label` strips U+FFFD, but the stored text is the *double-encoded* `Ï¿½` |
| Ethiopia | all | `cluster_features` | 21 distinct strings for 11 regions | Tigray/TIGRAY, Somalie/SOMALI, Diredwa/DIRE DAWA, Gambelia/GAMBELA. Per-wave values are internally consistent, so it bites only cross-wave pooling |
| Uganda | 2011-20 | `lsms_library/countries/Uganda/_/uganda.py:400` | at worst 0.22% of a wave (836 rows in 2019-20); 698 purchased + 514 produced + 79 in-kind across the panel | `warnings.warn("Dropping some unknown unit codes!")` -- the warning cannot be triaged because it does not say how many. Codes seen: 800, 801, 802, 996-999, plus keying slips (`123060`, `142090`, `156087`) |

## Why it matters

This is the binding constraint on cross-table price work, ranked first of 20
patterns by countries a single fix moves (7 of 8). Every source in the comparison
is a price *per unit `u`*, so two labels for one unit do not produce a wrong
number -- they produce **no number at all**, silently. Niger's `Tia`/`Tiya` split
meant the price per bowl, its most common non-metric unit, could never be matched
between the household and community instruments; GhanaLSS shipped four waves of
`food_acquired` off the very Preferred-Label axis the country curates, and the
regression survived because the delivered table was well-formed in every other
respect. There is no guard that can see this: `_assert_built_required_columns`
checks presence, `_audit_index_collapse` checks uniqueness, the null-read audit
checks content -- a valid string in the wrong vocabulary passes all three.

## Proposed fix

Per instance, and all of them are config, not core:

1. **GhanaLSS** -- re-apply the `_/unit_labels.org` Preferred-Label map in the four
   wave scripts, as 2016-17 already does (`359e52af`). Gate it on an index-uniqueness
   assertion after the rename: `food_acquired` is in `_ADDITIVE_MEASURE_COLUMNS`, so
   one duplicate index entry makes core SUM Quantity/Expenditure and re-derive
   `Price = Expenditure/Quantity` over the whole frame. Measured before the edit on the
   delivered 5,259,320-row table: **0 rows in duplicate groups**.
2. **Niger** -- both Original Labels -> `Tiya` (`4732a5eb`).
3. **Malawi** -- a mapping in the `u` table, not a rename of the raw labels.
4. **Mali** -- a `spellings:` entry for `Boite`/`Boîte`, or a row in Mali's `u` table.
5. **Ethiopia** -- canonicalise the `Other (Specify)` spacing in the `u` table; add
   the double-encoded mojibake sequence to `_clean_unit_label`'s strip; add `Region`
   to `categorical_mapping.org` as the strata labels already are.
6. **Uganda** -- print the count and the offending codes in the warning at `uganda.py:400`.
7. **Tanzania** -- see below; it needs the P19 sentinel reworked first.

## What must NOT be folded (state this before anyone "fixes" it)

- **Granularity is not spelling.** Malawi's `Heap (Large)` and a bare `Heap` are
  different units, not two spellings of one. Collapsing size-qualified labels onto
  their stem is the *opposite* defect (it is what makes Nigeria's community prices
  unusable -- see the C8 SIZE issue filed alongside this one).
- **Tanzania's `piece`/`Piece` fold is explicitly forbidden by the config, correctly.**
  `Tanzania/_/categorical_mapping.org:595-600`: *"Deliberately does NOT register the
  bare lowercase 'kg'/'piece' sentinel keys ... 'piece' is the framework collapse
  sentinel that must pass through unchanged on food_acquired ... Registering
  'piece' -> 'Piece' here would rewrite the live (u) axis value and regress
  food_acquired."* The sentinel is set by `tanzania.new_harmonize_units`, which is
  also the subject of the quantity-truncation issue filed alongside this one; the
  clean fix is a `u` sentinel that is not also a label, not a rename.
- **Some of it is not fixable.** GhanaLSS's price survey *weighs* the item while
  Section 8H records the container the respondent names, so only 3.5-11.2% of
  own-production rows are comparable in 1991-92 through 2012-13. That is two
  instruments measuring different things, and no mapping repairs it.

Surfaced by the five-source price comparison, 2026-09-08; per-country evidence in `slurm_logs/price_sources/<Country>/REPORT.org`; pattern `P08-unit-vocab` in `slurm_logs/price_sources/DATA_PROBLEMS.csv`.
title: The `u` axis is split by spelling in 7 countries: one unit under two labels (GhanaLSS 473,660 rows; Niger 26,000+)

Two sweeps of the package tree today found **433 workspace copies of source data files** under `lsms_library/countries/`, none tracked by git (gitignored), all confirmed by content md5 against the S3 remote and removed (manifests: `slurm_logs/intree_dvc_copies_2026-09-08.tsv`, 400 files / 1.31 GB; `slurm_logs/intree_sidecarless_2026-09-08.tsv`, 33 files / 0.05 GB). They fall in two classes with different risk:

1. **Beside their `.dvc` sidecar** (400 files, April-September). Harmless to correctness -- `get_dataframe` refuses them ("Refusing workspace copy of DVC-tracked file ... falling through to the DVC cache path") -- but they cost 1.3 GB on Lustre and one `UserWarning` per read.

2. **Without a sidecar** (33 files, dated 2026-06-03 and 06-07), in **ten stray wave directories at the countries root with the country segment missing**: `lsms_library/countries/{2009-10,2010-11,2011-12,2012-13,2013-14,2015-16,2018-19,2019-20,2020-21,2023-24}/Data/...` holding Nigeria `sect11*_plantingw*.dta` (with the WB zip's own `Post Planting Wave N/Agriculture/` subtree), Uganda `AGSEC6*.dta`, Tanzania `HH_SEC_H.dta`. A sidecar-less copy is the dangerous class: the reader's fallback chain is local file -> DVC -> WB, so a stray that lands on a path a script actually reads **shadows the DVC blob silently** (the #829 agent hit exactly this in its worktree: `Uganda/2019-20/Data/AGSEC5A.dta` with no sidecar, preferred over the cache). The root-level ones were inert only because no script resolves `../Data/` to `countries/2015-16/Data/`.

Both classes come from the World Bank zip fallback in `data_access.get_data_file` / `get_dataframe` (`populate_cache=True` "extract all files from the zip"), which extracts into the *tree*: the #829 agent produced 44 sidecar-beside copies in its worktree from documentation fetches alone, and the root-level directories are what that extraction does when the request path or cwd lacks the country segment (cf. #810, the cwd-relative `dvc.api.open` resolution).

Proposed:
- Extract WB zips into `data_root()` (the L1 cache's neighbourhood) or a temp dir, never into `countries_root()`; return the requested file's path from there. The package tree must not contain data (`CLAUDE.md`, "A `*.parquet` inside `countries_root()` is never read (GH #803)" -- the same rule for `.dta`).
- Make `get_dataframe` treat a sidecar-less data file inside `countries_root()` like it treats an in-tree parquet since #803: warn and ignore, never prefer.
- Have `lsms-library cache clear` (or a new `cache audit`) report in-tree data files, both classes, as it already reports in-tree parquets; and refuse to create `countries/<wave>/` paths with no country segment.

The 33-file class also means the earlier cleanup command in the library's own warning (`find ... -execdir test -e '{}.dvc' \; -delete`) misses the dangerous half by construction.
title: WB-zip fallback extracts source files into the package tree (433 found today, 33 without sidecars in stray countries/<wave>/ dirs); sidecar-less copies shadow the DVC cache

`Country(c).food_prices(units='unitprice')` (and `'kgprice'`) returns an **empty frame silently** for a country whose `food_acquired` has no `Price` column -- Ethiopia, Malawi, Mali, Niger, Nigeria, Tanzania all do this (`(0, 1)` frame, no warning, no error). Four of the eight price-comparison agents hit it independently (Malawi's REPORT D6, Nigeria, Niger, Tanzania) and each had to establish by hand that "0 rows" meant "the instrument never asks a price" rather than "a filter dropped everything".

The `units` docstring promises "NaN where the survey did not record a unit price" and "no silent fallback between modes" -- both honoured -- but an empty frame is not NaN-where-missing; it is the absence of the column dressed as the absence of rows. `food_expenditures(basis='total')` has the same shape of ambiguity on a country that records no in-kind value (it silently equals `'purchased'`), which the five-source protocol had to special-case.

Proposed: when the requested mode needs a column the table does not carry (`Price` for the `*price` modes), raise a `LabelUnavailableError`-style error naming the country and the missing column -- the pattern `labels=` already uses for a country that cannot honour a request (Contract B, PR #550) -- so `Feature('food_prices')(units='unitprice')` degrades loudly per country instead of concatenating empties. A `warnings.warn` is the minimum. Add the fact to `docs/guide/data-methods.md` under `units=`.
title: food_prices(units='unitprice'|'kgprice') returns an empty frame silently when food_acquired has no Price column (6 countries); should raise or warn like labels= does

body:
In Malawi `community_prices`, `u` and `NumberOfUnits` are **jointly blank on 38,506 of 82,635 rows (46%)** -- the price is recorded but neither the unit nor a count of units survives the build, so those rows have no per-unit price basis at all. The Malawi agent of the five-source price comparison dropped and counted them (`slurm_logs/price_sources/Malawi/REPORT.org`, defect D3); they are not "one piece" by default, they are unknown.

Seen while re-warming the shared cache from `cwd=/tmp` (2026-09-07, `d68f4b19`):

```
FAIL Armenia/household_roster YAMLValidationError: './pytest-of-ligon/pytest-64/popen-gw6/test_ensure_dvc_pulled_handles0/foo.dta.dvc' validation failed   457s
FAIL Armenia/household_characteristics  ...same...   319s
```

Armenia has no microdata, so a failure is expected -- but not this one, and not after 7 minutes. The source file is neither local nor in a sidecar, so `get_dataframe` reaches the `else:` branch at `lsms_library/local_tools.py:1390`:

```python
    else:
        try:
            with dvc.api.open(fn,mode='rb') as f:
```

`dvc.api.open` with no `repo=` resolves the DVC repository from the **current working directory**. From `/tmp` that is not the library's DVC root (`lsms_library/countries/`), and DVC then walks every `*.dvc` it can find under cwd: `/tmp/pytest-of-ligon/.../foo.dta.dvc` is a deliberately-malformed fixture from `test_ensure_dvc_pulled_handles...`, so the walk ends in `YAMLValidationError` -- after 300-450 s of scanning. The relative `./pytest-of-ligon/...` in the message is the tell (relative to cwd, not to the repo).

The same call at `local_tools.py:1667` (`from_dta`) has the same shape. Both predate the `get_dataframe` fallback chain and are exactly the anti-pattern CLAUDE.md lists ("`dvc.api.open(fn, mode='rb')` ... couples to DVC internals").

**Fix.** Pass the repo explicitly (`dvc.api.open(fn, repo=str(countries_root()), mode='rb')`) or, better, route this branch through the same `DVCFS.open` streaming fallback the sidecar branch already uses (`DVCFS` is built on the right root), and make a missing source fail fast with the WB-fallback error rather than a cwd walk. Add a test that runs `get_dataframe` on a non-existent source from a `tmp_path` cwd containing a malformed `*.dvc` and asserts no `YAMLValidationError` and sub-second failure.

Related: the CLAUDE.md gotcha "`get_dataframe('../Data/..')` from a chdir'd cwd falls through to `dvc.api.open` and raises -- use absolute paths" is this same bug seen from the other side.
title: get_dataframe's last-resort dvc.api.open() resolves the DVC repo from CWD (7-minute sidecar walk from /tmp, trips on pytest fixtures)
